title: Authenticated users can retrieve other users' non-public prayer requests by ID
reasoning: The viewset only requires authentication, and for retrieve/update/destroy it returns all PrayerRequest rows regardless of requester or status. There is no retrieve/object-permission check in the shown code, while the serializer exposes title, description, duration, status, moderation severity, counts, and owner state. That means any logged-in user who can guess or enumerate an ID can GET another user's pending, rejected, completed, or deleted request, including content that was never approved for public display.
reproduction: Create a pending_moderation PrayerRequest for user A, authenticate as user B, then GET /api/prayer-requests/{id}/. The queryset includes the object and the serializer returns its content.
recommendation: Restrict non-list object access to approved active requests unless the requester is the current user or the current user has staff/moderation privileges. Add an object-level permission or override get_queryset/get_object for retrieve separately from owner-only update/delete behavior.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included prayer API tests cover public prayers and prayer sets, not PrayerRequest retrieval authorization across owners and statuses.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add API tests asserting that user B receives 404/403 for user A's pending, rejected, and deleted prayer requests, while approved active requests remain accessible according to the intended public contract and owners can view their own requests.
minimumFixScope: PrayerRequestViewSet queryset/object permission logic and corresponding API tests.

history.reasoning: The original evidence paths still exist. The detail-ID part has been changed: prayers/views.py now has a retrieve branch at lines 334-341 that returns only staff-visible rows, the requester's own rows, or approved unexpired rows, and tests/test_prayer_requests.py lines 79-116 adds regression coverage for non-owner pending/rejected/deleted detail retrieval. However the same viewset still exposes non-public requests elsewhere: the list branch at prayers/views.py lines 280-328 starts from all PrayerRequest rows and, when a status query parameter is supplied, filters by status without requiring mine=true or staff. Because PrayerRequestSerializer.Meta at prayers/serializers.py lines 233-246 still exposes title, description, status, moderation_severity, etc., an authenticated non-owner can request /api/prayer-requests/?status=pending_moderation or rejected/deleted and receive other users' non-public request content. I attempted to run the targeted regression tests, but Docker was unavailable, so this is based on current code inspection rather than executed test results.
commands: pwd && rg -n "class PrayerRequestViewSet|def get_queryset|class PrayerRequestSerializer|class Meta|PrayerRequest" prayers tests -S

docker exec bahk_devcontainer-app-1 python manage.py test tests.test_prayer_requests.PrayerRequestAPITests.test_retrieve_hides_other_users_non_public_requests tests.test_prayer_requests.PrayerRequestAPITests.test_retrieve_allows_owner_and_active_approved_requests --settings=tests.test_settings

history.reasoning: The original evidence paths still exist, but the vulnerable behavior is no longer present in current code. prayers/views.py now scopes retrieve at lines 340-347 to staff, the requester, or approved non-expired requests, so an authenticated non-owner cannot GET another user's pending/rejected/deleted request by ID. The earlier follow-on list leak is also addressed: the list branch still accepts status filters, but lines 328-332 force non-staff, non-mine list responses back to approved non-expired requests. prayers/serializers.py still exposes sensitive request fields at lines 233-246, but those fields are only reached after the queryset authorization gates. Regression tests now exist in tests/test_prayer_requests.py for detail non-public hiding, list status-filter hiding, and owner/public retrieval behavior. I attempted to run the targeted tests, but Docker was not available in this environment, so the pass/fail result could not be executed here.
